_meta.note: Close the framework/Python gap: the domain adapters were node-only, so a pure-Python user with a framework backend (Agno/CrewAI) — exactly who the node-free Python port targets — couldn't use them without installing Node. Fix by making the adapters a genuine PARITY surface: mirror each in Python under py/src/heartbeat/adapters/{code,docs}/ (stdlib-only, importable + `python3 -m ...` CLI), proven node == python on the SAME fixtures. Parity is BYTE-IDENTICAL for the deterministic outputs (deplint findings+messages, context renderers) and SET-EQUAL for the maps (edge/row order can differ). The node adapters stay UNCHANGED (each runtime keeps its own impl; no cross-dependency). This also reverses the earlier 'adapters are not a parity surface' note — they now ARE, cross-checked like the core (project/resolve/lint/audit). Result: `context_cmd='python3 -m heartbeat.adapters.docs.context ...'` works with zero Node, so framework backends get the capability natively. Spec-first; adversarial review on every gate; keep tests/parity.sh + node + python suites green throughout.

phases.title: Code adapter in Python (deplint + codegraph map/context), node ≡ python

tasks.title: Author the code-adapter parity proofs (spec-first)
tasks.description: Spec-first, three proofs that MUST fail before the Python impls exist (python -m ... errors -> mismatch). Reuse the EXISTING node fixtures under plugin/adapters/code/fixtures/, and ADD a multi-finding fixture multi.dag.json + multi.codemap.json that yields >=2 MISSING and >=2 COLLISION findings (e.g. tasks TA,TB,TC,TD all requires []; edges [[symA,symB],[symA,symC]] so TA misses BOTH TB and TC; and TA,TD plus TB,TC share symbols so >=2 collisions) — so byte-parity actually PINS multi-finding emit ORDER (the one place a faithful-looking port could byte-diverge). (a) docs/howto/gate-examples/deplint-parity.sh — for each fixture (missing, redundant, collision, clean, transitive, MULTI) assert `node plugin/adapters/code/deplint.js <dag> <codemap>` and `PYTHONPATH=py/src python3 -m heartbeat.adapters.code.deplint <dag> <codemap>` produce BYTE-IDENTICAL stdout (full stdout, not just the summary line), AND that `--strict` yields identical EXIT CODES on each; marker DEPLINT-PARITY-OK. (b) codegraph-map-parity.sh — node codegraph-map.js and `python3 -m heartbeat.adapters.code.codegraph_map` on codegraph-rows.json produce the SAME codemap (compare edges as a SET + tasks as a map via a python one-liner, order-insensitive); marker CODEGRAPH-MAP-PARITY-OK. (c) codegraph-context-parity.sh — node codegraph-context.js and `python3 -m heartbeat.adapters.code.codegraph_context` on context.codemap.json TA produce BYTE-IDENTICAL stdout; marker CODEGRAPH-CONTEXT-PARITY-OK. set -euo pipefail + explicit exits; each fails before the Python module exists.

tasks.title: Implement deplint.py (byte-identical to deplint.js)
tasks.description: Create py/src/heartbeat/adapters/__init__.py, py/src/heartbeat/adapters/code/__init__.py, and py/src/heartbeat/adapters/code/deplint.py — a faithful port of plugin/adapters/code/deplint.js: same requires-transitive-closure logic, same MISSING/REDUNDANT/COLLISION detection, and BYTE-IDENTICAL stdout — the exact summary line `HB-CODE-DEPLINT: missing=N redundant=M collision=K` and the exact detail-line formats ('MISSING: A should require B  (x -> y)' with two spaces before the paren; 'REDUNDANT: A requires B but no direct code dependency between their symbols'; 'COLLISION: A and B share x,y (unordered — isolate or add a requires edge)') — iterating tasks in dag order so findings emit in the same order as node. CLI `python3 -m heartbeat.adapters.code.deplint <dag.json> <codemap.json> [--strict]` with the SAME exit-code contract (0 advisory; --strict -> 1 iff missing>0 or collision>0). Stdlib-only; imports nothing from heartbeat core; no node subprocess. Expose a pure `deplint(dag, codemap)` function too.

tasks.title: Implement codegraph_map.py + codegraph_context.py
tasks.description: Create py/src/heartbeat/adapters/code/codegraph_map.py (port of codegraph-map.js: rows {nodes,edges} -> {edges:[[qnFrom,qnTo]]}, same dependency-type allowlist calls/imports/inheritance, id->qualified_name; a harness-first readCodegraphDb using the stdlib `sqlite3` module — no shell-out; CLI `python3 -m heartbeat.adapters.code.codegraph_map <rows.json>` prints the codemap JSON compact — json.dumps(x, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=False) — matching node's JSON.stringify) and codegraph_context.py (port of codegraph-context.js: contextFor(codemap, taskId) -> the same subgraph text, BYTE-IDENTICAL to node; CLI `python3 -m heartbeat.adapters.code.codegraph_context <codemap.json> <TASKID>`). Stdlib-only; import nothing from core; no node subprocess. Expose pure functions (mapCodegraph, contextFor).

phases.title: Docs adapter in Python (map + context), node ≡ python

tasks.title: Author the docs-adapter parity proofs (spec-first)
tasks.description: Spec-first, two proofs that MUST fail before the Python docs impls exist, reusing the EXISTING node fixtures under plugin/adapters/docs/fixtures/. (a) docs/howto/gate-examples/docs-map-parity.sh — node docs-map.js and `python3 -m heartbeat.adapters.docs.docs_map` on the fixture corpus produce the SAME codemap (edges as a SET, tasks as a map — order-insensitive, since file-scan order differs across runtimes/OS); marker DOCS-MAP-PARITY-OK. (b) docs-context-parity.sh — node docs-context.js and `python3 -m heartbeat.adapters.docs.docs_context` on (corpus, docs.codemap.json, **intro**) — intro cites TWO sections (background + method), so this pins multi-section render ORDER — produce BYTE-IDENTICAL stdout; also check the single-cite case (results); marker DOCS-CONTEXT-PARITY-OK. set -euo pipefail + explicit exits; each fails before the Python module exists. (deplint parity is already covered by PA — the docs adapter reuses the same deplint.)

Stdlib-only (os, re, json); import nothing from core; no node subprocess. Expose pure functions (citationMap, citedContext).

phases.title: Framework availability + docs/skills + flip the parity-notes stance

tasks.title: Author the node-free availability proof (spec-first)
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/adapters-nodefree.sh — proves the adapter capability is available with PROVABLY ZERO Node. It builds a PATH that EXCLUDES node by filtering out every PATH entry that contains a node executable (iterate $PATH, drop any dir with an -x node) — NOT a hardcoded `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin` (node may live in /usr/bin). Then, inside that stripped env, it FIRST asserts `command -v node` FAILS (fail the proof loudly if node is still reachable — otherwise the test is vacuous), and only then runs the Python adapters: (1) `python3 -m heartbeat.adapters.docs.docs_map <corpus>`, `... docs.docs_context <corpus> <codemap> intro`, and `... code.deplint <dag> <codemap>` all produce their expected output; (2) a python context_cmd feeds the executor — with HB_EXEC_CONTEXT_CMD='python3 -m heartbeat.adapters.docs.docs_context <corpus> <codemap> results', `executor.assemble_context` injects the cited text — all with node off PATH. Marker ADAPTERS-NODEFREE-OK; fails before the Python adapters exist. Also add an ON-DEMAND ollama demo tests/real-docs-context-py.sh: same as real-docs-context.sh but the context_cmd is the PYTHON provider (node-free) driving a real ollama backend; skips without ollama; NOT gated.

Update docs/howto/feed-code-context-to-stage-b.md (and the docs how-to) to show the python context_cmd. IMPORTANT: update docs/howto/keep-the-runtimes-in-parity.md to REFERENCE the new adapter parity proofs by name (deplint-parity.sh, codegraph-map-parity.sh, codegraph-context-parity.sh, docs-map-parity.sh, docs-context-parity.sh) — so the self-audit's referenced-proof integrity enforces their existence AND wiring.
